chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to me, saying: Yaqoob ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Aban ibn Taqlib, from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali, from Salman al-Farsi - may God have mercy on him,

he said: I entered upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while Al-Hussein (peace be upon him) was on his thighs, and he was kissing his eyes and pressing his lips, and he was saying: 'You are the Master, son of the Master; you are the Imam, son of the Imam, Father of the Imams; you are the Proof, son of the Proof, Father of nine Proofs from your loins, the ninth of them is their Riser.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about Imam Al-Hussein and the nine Imams from his progeny?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Salman al-Farsi in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, serves as a foundational text for the doctrine of Imamah, explicitly linking the prophetic authority to the Ahl al-Bayt through the lineage of Imam al-Hussein. The Prophet’s declaration of 'nine proofs from his loins' establishes the number of Imams following him, culminating in the twelfth Imam, Al-Qa'im, who is central to Shia eschatology and the concept of the Hidden Imam. This narration underscores the divine designation (Nass) of the Imams, affirming their status as the spiritual and political successors to the Prophet.
